note: The contract `npm run check:self` enforces (SPEC.md §13). Each entry names a deliberately-broken fixture and the rule id that must fire on it. If a rule stops firing, the check that rule belongs to has rotted and check:self exits non-zero. `why` is there so whoever sees the failure knows what the fixture was defending, not just which assertion broke.

expected.why: a narrative file with no structured-data sibling must not build — the two-file pattern is the whole content model (SPEC.md §5.1)
a data file with no narrative sibling would render as a page with no prose
the filename is the URL slug; an id that disagrees with it makes every cross-reference ambiguous
same rule, enforced on the data side of the pair as well as the narrative side
the paired files must agree on identity, or the page's title and its specs describe different cars
an unresolved parent breaks breadcrumbs, the parent-chain walker, and the model hub's generation list
the kind/parent discriminator is the load-bearing piece of SPEC.md §5.1 — a trim hangs off a generation, never off a model hub
SPEC.md §5.1 requires every model hub to have at least one generation, even for a nameplate that only ever had one version, so templates never special-case a childless hub
brandRef drives the Origin taxonomy axis and the hero band's logo and accent colour — an unresolved one renders a car with no brand identity
SPEC.md §2 principle 3 — every number has a citation. A citation key pointing at nothing is a number with no provenance, which is the same thing as an uncited number

THE important one: a plausible-looking invented figure hiding behind status 'placeholder', an 'estimated' value that never says how it was estimated, and a 'verified' value with no source. This is precisely the failure mode 'no fabricated data, ever' exists to stop
an unlisted taxonomy tag must fail the build naming the vocabulary file to fix, rather than silently creating an orphan taxonomy page (SPEC.md §7)
every image's legal basis must be auditable rather than assumed (SPEC.md §10) — an image with no recorded licence must never reach the site
